title: Feelings & Health
description: Learn how to express how you feel and talk about health in Tamil.

exercises.explanation: Feelings and health words — essential for both casual chat and emergencies.

exercises.question: How do you say 'I'm not well' in Tamil?
exercises.explanation: 'Enakku noi irukku' = I'm sick / I'm not well. Literally 'to me illness is'. For minor discomfort say 'oru maari irukku'.
'Enakku doctor vendum' = I need a doctor. Or 'doctor vaangunga' = please get/call a doctor.

exercises.sentence: Inniki enakku romba ___. (Today I'm very happy.)
exercises.explanation: 'Inniki enakku romba sandhosham' = today I'm very happy. Romba = very, sandhosham = happy/happiness.
'Kashtam' means difficult, hard, or trouble. 'Romba kashtam' = very difficult / what a shame.

exercises.question: How do you respond to 'eppadi irukeenga?' (how are you?) if you're well?
exercises.explanation: 'Nallaa irukken, nandri' = I'm well, thank you — the natural response to 'how are you' in Tamil.
'Enakku romba sandhosham' = I am very happy. Enakku = to me, romba = very, sandhosham = happiness.
'Hospital enga irukku?' = where is the hospital? — one of the most important emergency phrases.
